reason: The NN K loop has a visible address dependency: each iteration loads from x0 and x3, advances both pointers, issues four ordered FMOPAs, then decrements and branches. This makes pointer generation and loop control candidates for investigation, but the assembly does not show which limits throughput. Rank the NEON transpose first because it changes the timed conversion in the previously measured, non-promoted TB path; those whole-call results do not show that transpose caused the regression. Four-step unrolling targets visible loop control, but prior unroll results do not establish a gain. TA adds a timed transpose while retaining generated B packing and adding A packing, so its complete path has substantial added work. Padding has no supplied cache-geometry evidence; half-band packing adds packing work and resembles an unpromoted traversal; fused transpose repeats A-tile conversion across 16 panels. The K-pair proposal appears to repeat the measured two-step unroll's load-two-then-compute-two schedule, so it ranks last pending proof of a distinct instruction schedule.
